name: Worst Mistakes of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$, the known target can be predicted without error. For $n\ge2$, predict zero until the first positive label appears; that label identifies the target singleton, after which all predictions are correct. Thus at most one mistake occurs, even if coordinates repeat. For the lower bound, choose a sequence consisting of one coordinate. Both labels occur among the possible singleton targets, so any prediction can be falsified by a target consistent with that label. Knowledge of the entire presented sequence cannot avoid this first mistake.
